\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Low Degree}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Applications.LowDegree
\section{Overview}
Cube hypercontractivity controls moment growth and concentration for functions of bounded Fourier degree. Both one-sided and two-sided anticoncentration estimates accompany properties of the stable-cube probability graph.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Squared first-to-second norm comparison]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lowDegree_l1_l2_sq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.HasDegreeAtMost, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.low_degree_l1_l2_sq, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.has_degree_at_most, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.parseval, BooleanAnalysis.walsh_expansion}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p116-b005}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube of Fourier degree at most $k\in\mathbb N$. Then $e^{-2k}\mathbb Ef^2\le(\mathbb E|f|)^2$.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{5}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and $-1\le\rho\le1$. On the Boolean cube $\{0,1\}^n$, assign
the ordered pair $(x,y)$ weight
$W(x,y)=2^{-n}\prod_{i=1}^n(1+\rho\sigma(x_i)\sigma(y_i))/2$, where $\sigma(0)=1$
and $\sigma(1)=-1$. These weights are nonnegative and symmetric, each row sums to
$2^{-n}$, and the sum over all ordered pairs is one.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{6}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a real-valued function on the uniform Boolean cube, and
let $k\in\mathbb N$. Suppose every nonzero Fourier coefficient of $f$ is supported on a
set of size at most $k$, and that $\operatorname{Var}(f)>0$. Then $\dfrac{9}{16\cdot
9^k}\le \Pr\!\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(f)}}{2}<|f-\E f|\right)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Higher norms of cube polynomials]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lowDegree_norm_ge_two}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeLpNorm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.general_one_function_hypercontractivity, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.l2Norm_noiseOp_le, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_compose, BooleanAnalysis.has_degree_at_most, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.l2Norm, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.walsh_expansion}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p262-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p247-b006
}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube of Fourier degree at most $k\in\mathbb N$, and let $q\ge2$. Then $\|f\|_q\le(\sqrt{q-1})^k\|f\|_2$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a real-valued function on the uniform Boolean cube, and
let $k\in\mathbb N$. Suppose every nonzero Fourier coefficient of $f$ is supported on a
set of size at most $k$. For real numbers $p,q$ with $0<p<2<q$, the norms defined by
$\|f\|_r=(\E|f|^r)^{1/r}$ satisfy $\|f\|_2\le
\exp\!\left(\dfrac{kq(2-p)}{2p}\right)\|f\|_p$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Lower norms of cube polynomials]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lowDegree_norm_le_two}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeLpNorm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lowDegree_norm_le_two_aux, BooleanAnalysis.has_degree_at_most, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.l2Norm}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p248-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p262-b006
}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube of Fourier degree at most $k\in\mathbb N$, and let $1\le p\le2$. Then $\|f\|_2\le\exp((2/p-1)k)\|f\|_p$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Lower bound for the concentration parameter]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.concentration_parameter}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ConcentrationAux.concentration_parameter}
\difficulty{1}
Let $k$ be a positive integer and $t\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $(\sqrt{2e})^k\le t$. Then
$t>0$ and $t^{2/k}/e\ge2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Optimized concentration moment identity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.concentration_optimized_moment}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ConcentrationAux.concentration_optimized_moment}
\difficulty{1}
Let $k$ be a positive integer and let $t>0$. Set $q=t^{2/k}/e$, where $e=\exp(1)$. Then
$\bigl((\sqrt q)^k/t\bigr)^q=\exp\bigl(-k t^{2/k}/(2e)\bigr)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Tail bound for low degree]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lowDegree_concentration}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.concentration_optimized_moment, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.concentration_parameter, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeLpNorm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeProbability, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeProbability_le_cubeLpNorm_div_rpow, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_rpow_abs_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lowDegree_norm_ge_two, BooleanAnalysis.has_degree_at_most, BooleanAnalysis.l2Norm}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p263-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p263-b003
}

\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a real-valued function on the uniform Boolean cube, and
let $k\in\mathbb N$ with $k>0$. Suppose every nonzero Fourier coefficient of $f$ is
supported on a set of size at most $k$, and $\|f\|_2>0$. For every $t\in\mathbb R$ such
that $(\sqrt{2e})^k\le t$, we have $\Pr\bigl(t\|f\|_2\le |f|\bigr)\le
\exp\!\left(-\dfrac{k}{2e}t^{2/k}\right)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bounded-degree one-sided anticoncentration]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lowDegree_oneSided_anticoncentration}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.centered_abs_expect_sq_le, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeProbability, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeVariance, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.has_degree_at_most_sub_const, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lowDegree_l1_l2_sq, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.expect_const, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.expect_sub, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.has_degree_at_most, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p263-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p263-b006
}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube of Fourier degree at most $k\in\mathbb N$, with positive variance. Then $e^{-2k}/4\le\Pr(\mathbb Ef<f)$.
\end{theorem}
